subject: english
title: Mangrove Fact Finders
objective: Find the topic and important facts in a short informational text.
introduction: Milo reads a short text about mangrove trees near the sea. Can you separate the topic from facts the text gives?

vocabulary.definition: a tree that grows in salty coastal water
underground parts that hold soil in place
a safe place where living things can hide

activities.instruction: Read the text and notice its topic and supporting facts.
activities.content: Informational texts teach about a real topic. Look for the topic, facts, and details that explain it.

feedback.retry: Reread the text and check whether the detail names the topic or supports it.

activities.prompt: Learn how facts explain the topic of an informational text.
activities.narration: This text is about mangrove trees. It explains that their roots hold soil, the trees shelter living things, and they grow near the sea.
activities.guideHint: Ask what the whole text is mostly about, then find facts that support it.
activities.accessibilityAlternative: This text is about mangrove trees. It explains that their roots hold soil, the trees shelter living things, and they grow near the sea.

activities.instruction: Tap the topic and facts supported by the text.

feedback.retry: Check the text for the exact topic or supporting fact.

activities.prompt: Find details that belong to the mangrove text.
activities.narration: The topic is the main subject; facts give true details about that subject.
activities.guideHint: Look for the repeated subject and the details connected to it.
activities.accessibilityAlternative: The topic is the main subject; facts give true details about that subject.

activities.instruction: Sort mangrove-text details from other statements.

feedback.retry: Reread the text and find evidence before sorting again.

activities.prompt: Sort each card by whether the text supports it.
activities.narration: A supported detail matches the mangrove text; other statements belong to a different topic or are opinions.
activities.guideHint: Compare the card with the text about mangrove trees.
activities.accessibilityAlternative: A supported detail matches the mangrove text; other statements belong to a different topic or are opinions.

activities.instruction: Tap the subject repeated across the informational text.

content.instruction: What is the topic of the text?

feedback.retry: Check which choice connects to every fact in the text.

activities.prompt: Choose the topic Milo is reading about.
activities.narration: The topic names what the whole text is about, not one unrelated object.
activities.guideHint: Look for the subject shared by all the facts.
activities.accessibilityAlternative: The topic names what the whole text is about, not one unrelated object.

activities.instruction: Match each detail to the role it plays in the text.

pairs.right: fact about keeping shore soil in place
fact about safe places for living things
fact about where the trees live

feedback.retry: Check whether the detail names the topic or supports it.

activities.prompt: Match the topic or fact with the clue it provides.
activities.narration: The topic names the subject, while facts explain where mangroves grow and how they help living things.
activities.guideHint: Read the detail and ask whether it is the subject or evidence.
activities.accessibilityAlternative: The topic names the subject, while facts explain where mangroves grow and how they help living things.

activities.instruction: Put the topic-and-fact checks in order.

feedback.retry: Check that you named the topic, found facts, and connected each fact.

activities.prompt: Order the steps for finding the topic and evidence.
activities.narration: Readers identify the repeated subject, then choose facts that explain it.
activities.guideHint: Begin by reading the whole text.
activities.accessibilityAlternative: Readers identify the repeated subject, then choose facts that explain it.

items.prompt: Milo tells a friend what his informational text is mostly about. Which topic is correct?
items.explanation: Mangrove trees are the subject repeated across the text, so they are the topic.

items.prompt: Milo underlines a sentence that the text truly states. Which is a fact from the text?
items.explanation: The text says mangrove roots hold soil in place; that statement is supported.

items.prompt: Milo checks whether a detail belongs in his notes. Which detail is NOT in the text?
items.explanation: The text describes roots, shelter, and coastal growth, but it never says mangroves can fly.

items.prompt: Milo sees a statement that tells a feeling instead of evidence. Which is an opinion?
items.explanation: Boring tells someone’s feeling about mangroves; the other choices state information from the text.

items.prompt: Milo adds one sentence to a text about mangroves. Which sentence belongs?
items.explanation: Mangroves help protect the shore stays on the text’s topic and gives a related fact.
